regions.explanation: From 1.84s to 5.65s (“party but a celebration of freedom— symbolizing an end as …”), 3 pause(s) at punctuation shrank from 393 ms to 0 ms on average. Pauses at punctuation mark the end of an idea and give the audience time to absorb it; running through them merges separate thoughts into one stream. Fix: Hold a clear pause at each punctuation mark, about as long as the reference.

From 15.64s to 17.33s (“world is very different”), articulation rate slowed to 5.11 syll/s against 6.86 syll/s in the reference (-26%); that is 1.4× the reference speaker's natural word-to-word variation. Stretched words without matching emphasis read as hesitation and dilute the rhythm of the phrase; the audience's attention drifts between content words. Fix: Tighten these words to the reference pace; keep length only on the stressed word.
